little.twist: Lina asks for more after you shook hands, and nothing glows to help.
little.can_now: say why people swap, make a fair swap that is good for both, say no kindly to an unfair one and keep a swap they agreed

steps.say: The Market Square! Today you swap things at the swap stall. A fair swap makes both people happy.
You have lots of apples. Lina has lots of pears. Why swap?

choices.text: So you both have apples and pears
To take all of Lina's pears
choices.why: A swap gives as well as takes.
A fair swap is good for both!

steps.done: People swap and trade so everyone gets what they need.

steps.say: Lina offers {swap_n} pears for {swap_n} apples. Put {swap_n} apples on the swap table.
steps.done: {swap_n} apples for {swap_n} pears.

steps.say: Is {swap_n} apples for {swap_n} pears a fair swap?

choices.text: Yes: the same for both of us

choices.why: You both give the same and you are both happy: that's fair!

steps.done: Fair for both.

steps.say: Shake hands on it!
steps.done: A swap agreed is a promise.

steps.say: After you shook hands, Lina asks for 2 more apples. What do you say?

choices.text: We agreed {swap_n} for {swap_n}: that's our swap

choices.why: A swap is a promise for both. Say kindly what you agreed.
Talk kindly: grabbing is never the way.

steps.done: Lina smiles: "You're right. A deal is a deal!"

steps.say: Take your pears.
steps.done: Now you both have apples and pears.

steps.say: Take your pears.
steps.done: Now you both have apples and pears.

steps.say: Mo offers 1 sticker for ALL your apples. What do you say?

choices.text: No, thank you. 1 apple for 1 sticker?

choices.why: Then you'd have no apples left, for one sticker. Ask for a fair swap.

steps.done: "OK, 1 for 1!" Mo grins. Fair is better.

steps.say: Rosa has a little jar you like. She would love one of your drawings. You are both happy to swap. Is it fair?

choices.text: Yes: we both get something we want
No: things must be the same
choices.why: A swap is fair when both people are happy with it.

steps.done: A drawing for a jar: both happy!

steps.say: Say thank you to Lina for a fair swap.
steps.done: Lina wants to swap with you again!

steps.say: Well done! You swapped fairly, said no kindly to an unfair swap, and kept your word.

check.say: Why do people swap and trade?
1 sticker for ALL your apples. Fair?

name_it.title: Swapping fairly
lines: A fair swap is good for both.
Say kindly what you would like.
No, thank you, to an unfair swap.
A swap agreed is a promise.

little.try_real: Swap a toy or a book with a friend, fairly, with a grown-up's OK.

sources.fact: Voluntary exchange happens only when both sides expect to gain.
sources.source: Council for Economic Education, Voluntary National Content Standards in Economics (2010), standard 5

middle.skill: Supply and demand: why prices move
middle.twist: The festival and many cake sellers on the same day, and nothing glows to help.
middle.can_now: read a price board, say why prices go up or down (supply and demand), buy and sell with change, haggle politely and explain why specialising and trading makes both richer

steps.say: The Market Square! Buddy merchants sell here, and the Price Board shows today's prices. Prices move for reasons you can see.
Read the Price Board.
steps.done: Wheat {wheat_base}, flour {flour_price}, apples {apple_base}, honey {honey_base}, cakes {cake_base}: the usual prices.

steps.label: A dry summer
steps.say: Watch a dry summer go by: hardly any rain falls on the wheat fields.
steps.done: The wheat grew short and thin.

steps.say: Less wheat grew, but people still want bread. What happens to the price of wheat?

choices.why: Less to sell and the same people buying: the price goes up.
When there is less to sell, buyers offer more for it.

steps.done: Wheat is {wheat_dry} now. Less supply: a higher price.

steps.say: It's the festival! Everyone wants cakes today. What happens to the price of cakes?

choices.why: More people want cakes than usual: the price goes up.
More buyers for the same cakes: the price goes up.

steps.done: Cakes are {cake_festival} today. More demand: a higher price.

steps.say: The festival, and many more cake sellers came too! What happens to the price of cakes?

choices.text: It changes less: the two pull opposite ways

choices.why: More sellers pull the price down while more buyers pull it up.
There are more cakes than ever: lots of sellers!

steps.done: More buyers and more sellers: the price stays about {cake_base}.

steps.say: Four more farmers bring apples to sell today. What happens to the price of apples?

choices.why: Lots of apples and sellers wanting buyers: sellers lower their prices.
With so many apples to choose from, prices fall.

steps.done: Apples are {apple_many} today. More supply: a lower price.

steps.say: Find apples on the Price Board, and read why the price moved.
steps.done: The board says why: many sellers came.

steps.say: Let's buy flour from Tomas the miller.
steps.done: Here's Tomas's stall.

steps.say: Flour is {flour_price} coins a sack. Pay Tomas {flour_total} coins for {flour_words}.
steps.done: "Thank you!" Tomas gives you the flour.

steps.say: Ana's apples are {apple_base} coins a bag. You want {haggle_bags} bags: {haggle_full} coins. How do you ask for a better price?

choices.why: Rude words make people stop wanting to trade with you.
That's not a deal: both sides should win.

steps.done: Ana smiles: "{haggle_ask}, as you're buying {haggle_bags}. Deal!"

steps.say: Shake hands on the deal.
steps.done: A fair deal, politely made.

steps.say: In a day you bake {sp_you_loaves} loaves OR pick {sp_you_bags} bags of apples. Ana picks {sp_ana_bags} bags OR bakes {sp_ana_loaves} loaves. If you only bake, and she only picks?

choices.why: That's what you make doing half of each. Doing what you each do best makes more!
Each doing their best thing makes more of both.

steps.done: More of both! Swap {sp_trade} loaves for {sp_trade} bags, and you each have more than before.

steps.say: At the festival a customer buys a cake at {cake_festival} and pays with a 10 coin. Give {cake_change} coins change.
steps.done: {cake_festival} and {cake_change} make 10.

steps.label: Autumn's harvest
steps.say: The seasons pass, and autumn brings the harvest.
steps.done: The fields are full of wheat.

steps.say: A big wheat harvest: lots of wheat to sell. What happens to the price of wheat?

choices.why: Lots of wheat for the same buyers: the price falls.
The dry summer is over: now there is plenty.

steps.done: Wheat is {wheat_autumn} now: supply and demand, with causes you can see.

steps.say: You read the Price Board, saw why prices move, bought, haggled politely, specialised and traded. Both sides richer!

check.say: Less wheat grows this year. Its price...
Many sellers bring apples. The price of apples...
A polite way to ask for a better price:

choices.text: Could you do 4 if I buy 3?

check.say: Each doing what they do best, then trading...

name_it.title: Supply and demand
lines: Less to sell, the same buyers: the price goes up.
More to sell, or many sellers: the price goes down.
More buyers: the price goes up.
Doing what you do best and trading makes both richer.
Haggle politely: both sides should win.
name_it.source: The Council for Economic Education's standards (2010) and the Bank of England's economics teaching

middle.try_real: With a grown-up at a market or a shop, find a price that changed this season, and guess why.

sources.fact: Prices send signals: when supply or demand changes, market prices adjust.
sources.source: Council for Economic Education, Voluntary National Content Standards in Economics (2010), standards 7 and 8

sources.fact: Specialising in what you make at the lowest cost and trading increases production and consumption.
sources.source: Council for Economic Education, Voluntary National Content Standards in Economics (2010), standard 6

sources.fact: Markets, prices, supply and demand for school students.
sources.source: Bank of England, Economics in practice (teaching resource)

big.skill: Trading honestly, and why gambling loses
big.twist: A new dice game pays 5 for a 6: work out what it still takes. And nothing glows to help.
big.can_now: buy when there is plenty and sell when it is scarce honestly, keep only the stock they can store and sell, spread across goods, and explain with averages why games of chance lose over time

steps.say: Trading for the long run: buy and sell honestly, keep a stock, spread out, and see why gambling loses. Pretend coins and pretend counters only.
It's autumn's harvest. Read the apples on the Price Board.
steps.done: Apples are {apple_autumn} a bag now. In winter they are usually about {apple_winter}.

steps.say: What is an honest way to trade apples?

choices.text: Buy some now, store them well, sell in winter at a fair price
Sell old apples as fresh ones
choices.why: That's a lie: customers find out, and never trust you again.

choices.text: Buy every apple so nobody else can
choices.why: That's unfair to everyone, and your shed would overflow.

steps.done: Buying when there's plenty and selling when it's scarce is honest, and it helps: there are apples in winter.

steps.say: Your shed holds {shed} bags. Apples keep about 3 months, and you can sell about {per_month} bags a month. How many bags do you buy?

choices.why: Apples you can't sell before they go soft are money wasted.
Too few: your customers will want more.

steps.done: {stock} bags: what you can store and sell before they go soft.

steps.say: Carry the bags into your shed.
steps.done: Stocked up!

steps.label: Winter
steps.say: Autumn turns to winter. Few apples are left in the market.
steps.done: Winter.

steps.say: Apples are {apple_winter} a bag now. A customer buys {sale_bags} bags and pays with a 20 note. Give {sale_change} coins change.
steps.done: {sale_total} and {sale_change} make 20. A fair price, honestly earned.

steps.say: Spread your trading: put some stock in each basket, wheat, apples and honey.
steps.done: Three baskets, not one.

steps.say: A storm flattens the wheat fields: no wheat to sell for a while. How is your business?

choices.text: All right: apples and honey still sell

choices.why: That happens with only one basket. You have three!
A storm hurts the wheat traders. Spreading out keeps you steady.

steps.done: Spreading out keeps you steady when one thing goes wrong.

steps.say: At the fair, Pip-pop has a pretend game: "Pay 1 counter. Throw a 6 and get {dice_pays} back!" Let's find out what happens, with pretend counters. Nobody bets anything.
Throw the dice 6 times, and count the sixes.
steps.done: {dice_sixes} sixes in 6 throws.

steps.say: On a fair dice, how often does a 6 come up, over many throws?

choices.why: A dice has 6 faces, and each comes up as often as the others.
The dice can't know what you need: every throw is new.

steps.done: About 1 in 6.

steps.label: 600 throws
steps.say: Now watch 600 throws, drawn as a chart: 600 counters paid, and {dice_pays} back for each 6.
steps.done: The line went down and down.

steps.say: The line ends {chart_lost} counters down. Why?

choices.text: A 6 pays {dice_pays}, but it takes about 6 throws to get one
Bad luck: it will turn soon
choices.why: Every throw is new: the dice don't remember. The line keeps going down.
How you throw doesn't change a fair dice.

steps.done: Games like this are made to keep more than they give. Over time, the player always ends up with less.

steps.say: A new game pays {expert_pays} for a 6. In {expert_throws} throws you pay {expert_throws} counters and get about {expert_back} back. About how many are lost?

choices.why: {expert_back} back for {expert_throws} paid: still a loss.
That's what comes back. Take it away from {expert_throws}.

steps.done: Still a loss: the game always keeps a little more than it gives.

steps.say: Which one is gambling?

choices.text: Paying for a chance to win a prize

choices.why: That's trading: you give people something they want.
Saving keeps your money, and it grows a little.

steps.done: Gambling is paying for a chance to win. Trading and saving are not gambling.

steps.say: You traded honestly, kept a stock, spread out, and saw why gambling loses over time. For real money, talk to a grown-up you trust.

check.say: Over many throws, a game that pays back less than it takes...

choices.text: always takes more than it gives
keeps you steady if one goes wrong

check.say: Buying apples in autumn and selling them honestly in winter is...
A fair dice shows a 6 about...
